verdict: Strong 28-day ROAS holds; last-week dip is revenue timing, not decay.
narrative: Over the last 28 days, your Meta ads returned $4.05 for every $1 spent on $1,554.55 in total spend — a solid result. The sharp drop in 7-day return on ad spend (down 43.57% versus the prior 7 days) looks alarming on the surface, but traces directly to three zero-revenue days within the window, not a fall in ad efficiency. Purchase volume was nearly flat across both periods; revenue just landed unevenly. To close a known attribution gap, purchase tracking is being repaired so reported figures better reflect actual sales going forward. Several deliverables — subscribe page rebuild, CRM flows, and monthly report — are due by tomorrow, September 30, and those will sharpen visibility heading into October.

highlights.phrase: return on ad spend across the full 28-day period
purchases driven by Meta ads this period
Google Business Profile actions (calls, direction requests, and site clicks) in the last 28 days

watch_item.issue: Purchase tracking fires inconsistently, meaning some sales are not being counted in reported revenue.
watch_item.fix: Tracking is being corrected now; once live, reported ROAS will more accurately reflect true sales performance.
